title: Geometry of Straight Lines
summary: Use angle relationships on straight lines, around points, at intersecting lines and with parallel lines to solve multi-step problems with reasons, including algebraic angle problems and proving that lines are parallel.

notes.caption: Facts and their reasons
rows: Angles on a straight line add up to $180^\circ$
Angles around a point add up to $360^\circ$
Corresponding angles are equal (if lines are parallel)
Alternate angles are equal (if lines are parallel)
Co-interior angles add up to $180^\circ$ (if lines are parallel)
Angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$
Exterior angle = sum of the interior opposite angles

notes.text: To prove that lines are **parallel**, use the converses: equal corresponding angles (corresp ∠s =), equal alternate angles (alt ∠s =), or co-interior angles that add up to $180^\circ$ (co-int ∠s supp).
When angles are given as expressions, use an angle relationship to write an **equation**, solve it, and then substitute back to find the angles.

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem:
(a) Two angles on a straight line are $x$ and $2x + 30^\circ$. Find $x$.
(b) Two vertically opposite angles are $4x - 10^\circ$ and $2x + 40^\circ$. Find $x$ and the angle.
(c) Four angles around a point are $x$, $2x$, $3x$ and $90^\circ$. Find $x$.
steps: (a) $x + 2x + 30^\circ = 180^\circ$ (∠s on a str line), so $3x = 150^\circ$ and $x = 50^\circ$.
(b) $4x - 10^\circ = 2x + 40^\circ$ (vert opp ∠s), so $2x = 50^\circ$, $x = 25^\circ$ and each angle is $90^\circ$.

notes.title: Worked example 2: parallel lines with algebra
notes.problem: $AB \parallel CD$. Two co-interior angles are $3x + 20^\circ$ and $2x + 10^\circ$. Find $x$ and both angles.

notes.text: Harder problems need several steps. Sometimes it helps to draw an extra line (a **construction**) parallel to the given lines.

notes.title: Worked example 3: the zigzag
notes.problem: In the diagram, $AB \parallel CD$, $\hat{BEG} = 40^\circ$ and $\hat{DFG} = 30^\circ$. Calculate $x = \hat{EGF}$.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: If you add a construction line to a diagram, you must **state it** in your answer (e.g. "Construction: draw $GH \parallel AB$") before you use it.

notes.title: Worked example 4: proving the angle sum of a triangle
notes.problem: Use parallel lines to prove that the angles of $\triangle ABC$ add up to $180^\circ$.
steps: Construction: through $A$, draw line $DE$ parallel to $BC$, with $D$ on the same side as $B$.

notes.title: Worked example 5
notes.problem: A transversal cuts lines $PQ$ and $RS$. Two corresponding angles are $3x + 10^\circ$ and $4x - 15^\circ$, and $x = 25^\circ$. Is $PQ \parallel RS$?
steps: The corresponding angles are equal, so $PQ \parallel RS$ (corresp ∠s =).

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: Do not assume lines are parallel just because they look parallel. Unless parallel lines are given (or marked with arrows), you must **prove** it before using corresponding, alternate or co-interior angles.

items: Know every angle fact and the exact reason to write for it.
Use the relationships to set up and solve equations for unknown angles.
For complicated figures, work step by step and consider a construction parallel to the given lines.
Prove lines parallel with equal corresponding or alternate angles, or supplementary co-interior angles.
State any construction before using it.

questions.prompt: Two angles on a straight line are $x$ and $2x + 30^\circ$. Calculate $x$, in degrees.
Two vertically opposite angles are $4x - 10^\circ$ and $2x + 40^\circ$. Calculate $x$, in degrees.
In the zigzag diagram in the notes, $\hat{BEG} = 40^\circ$ and $\hat{DFG} = 30^\circ$. Calculate $x = \hat{EGF}$, in degrees.
Which reason correctly justifies that two alternate angles are equal?
questions.explanation: Alternate angles are equal **because** the lines are parallel, so the reason must mention the parallel lines. "alt ∠s =" is the reason for proving lines parallel.

questions.prompt: Two lines are cut by a transversal and two co-interior angles are $95^\circ$ and $85^\circ$. The lines are parallel.
questions.explanation: $95^\circ + 85^\circ = 180^\circ$, so the co-interior angles are supplementary and the lines are parallel.

questions.prompt: Four angles around a point are $x$, $2x$, $3x$ and $90^\circ$. Calculate $x$, in degrees.
$AB \parallel CD$. Two corresponding angles are $3x + 5^\circ$ and $5x - 25^\circ$. Find $x$.
An exterior angle of a triangle is $130^\circ$, and one of the interior opposite angles is $70^\circ$. Calculate the other interior opposite angle, in degrees.
questions.explanation: Exterior angle = sum of interior opposite angles: $130 - 70 = 60$.

questions.prompt: Match each reason with the fact it stands for.

pairs.right: Corresponding angles between parallel lines are equal
Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal
Co-interior angles between parallel lines add to 180°
Angles on a straight line add to 180°

questions.explanation: Learn these abbreviations; they are expected in geometry answers.

questions.prompt: Two co-interior angles between parallel lines are $3x$ and $2x$. Calculate $x$, in degrees.
Three angles of $75^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $55^\circ$ can lie next to each other on a straight line.
A transversal cuts lines $PQ$ and $RS$. Two corresponding angles are $68^\circ$ and $72^\circ$. What can you conclude?
questions.explanation: If the lines were parallel, the corresponding angles would be equal. They are not, so the lines are not parallel.

questions.prompt: $AB \parallel CD$. Point $E$ is on $AB$, $F$ is on $CD$, and $G$ lies between the lines (as in the zigzag diagram). $\hat{BEG} = 40^\circ$ and $\hat{DFG} = 30^\circ$. Calculate $\hat{EGF}$, giving reasons.
Through vertex $A$ of $\triangle ABC$, line $DE$ is drawn parallel to $BC$. Use this to prove that $\hat{A} + \hat{B} + \hat{C} = 180^\circ$.
questions.memo:
$\hat{DAB} = \hat{B}$ (alt ∠s; $DE \parallel BC$) ✓ (1)
$\hat{EAC} = \hat{C}$ (alt ∠s; $DE \parallel BC$) ✓ (1)
$\hat{DAB} + \hat{BAC} + \hat{EAC} = 180^\circ$ (∠s on a str line) ✓ (1)
So $\hat{B} + \hat{A} + \hat{C} = 180^\circ$ ✓ (1)

questions.prompt: $AB \parallel CD$. Two co-interior angles are $3x + 20^\circ$ and $2x + 10^\circ$. Calculate $x$ and both angles.
A transversal cuts lines $PQ$ and $RS$. Two corresponding angles are $3x + 10^\circ$ and $4x - 15^\circ$. If $x = 25^\circ$, is $PQ \parallel RS$? Explain.
questions.memo:
$3(25) + 10 = 85^\circ$ ✓ (1)
$4(25) - 15 = 85^\circ$ ✓ (1)
The corresponding angles are equal, so $PQ \parallel RS$ (corresp ∠s =) ✓ (1)
